body:
Owner question (post-01M1DEBZJR3Z6DXCWFWFCZ9NKX): is RecallSegmenter heuristics or something more sophisticated?

Honest answer: heuristics. The object's own comment says so: a deterministic, rule-based baseline — regex clause splitters (and/then/but/so/because/…), cue lexicons for hedges and discourse function, a shallow proposition sketch. Every rule is meant to be replaced by a provider behind the same RecallGraph contract. None of it is a scientific claim about recall language.

The sophisticated piece is not this step. Alignment is GraphHsmm (partial, unbalanced, hierarchical). Segmentation just has to exist, and be reproducible, so the aligner has units to work on.

For the docs editor: do not describe RecallSegmenter.segment as if it were the product. Say it cuts the transcript into idea units with a rule baseline, then the library's actual work is aligning those units to the story.
